of the country’s biggest political recruiters and thinkers, Dick Saslaw, predicted before the primary that Sinema would attract Republican women and independents.
“It’s what independents want and that’s why Sinema will win. It is not run at this time by our doctrinaire principles, because it's not an election about principles, it’s about getting policy results,” Saslaw said.
He predicted that McSally would exaggerate herself as a “fighting tribune” and was especially concerned about her commitment to the Senate Trump tax reform bill.
And, voila, it came to pass.
"In the very first week after I had received 48% of my statewide vote, Sen. Sinema voted against the Arizona Taxpayers - us!" wrote commentator Mark Bergreen, a partisan Republican who is incensed with liberals and tea party forces alike.
